{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study quantitatively compares genomic responses between mouse models and human patients for inflammatory diseases, reporting concordance rates (R2 values) and percentages of genes changing in the same direction. This directly addresses the concordance of animal model results with human clinical outcomes.",
  "arm": "disease-biology",
  "arm_evidence": "Here, we show that, although acute inﬂammatory stresses from different etiologies result in highly similar genomic responses in humans, the responses in corresponding mouse models correlate poorly with the human conditions and also, one another.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "sepsis-inflammation",
    "infectious-disease"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Genomic responses in mouse models poorly mimic human inﬂammatory diseases... The Inﬂammation and Host Response to Injury, Large Scale Collaborative Research Program has completed multiple studies on the genomic responses to systemic inﬂammation in patients and human volunteers as well as murine models",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The Inﬂammation and Host Response to Injury, Large Scale Collaborative Research Program has completed multiple studies on the genomic responses to systemic inﬂammation in patients and human volunteers as well as murine models... GEO was queried for studies in the white blood cells of additional severe acute inﬂammatory diseases [sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and infections] in human and mouse.",
  "species": [
    "mouse"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "Genomic responses in mouse models poorly mimic human inﬂammatory diseases... expression analysis on analogous samples from well-established mouse models of trauma, burns, and endotoxemia",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "Among genes changed signiﬁcantly in humans, the murine orthologs are close to random in matching their human counterparts (e.g., R2 between 0.0 and 0.1)."
}
